# joinpoint: Trend Analysis by Joinpoint Regression

***joinpoint*** fits joinpoint (segmented line) regression models for
trend analysis (Kim et al. 2000). It finds the points in time at which a
trend changes, summarizes each period by its annual percent change
(APC), fixed periods by the average annual percent change (AAPC), and
draws publication quality figures with ggplot2.

It covers the classical least squares joinpoint model with its error
models, model selection rules and confidence intervals, together with
the extensions of the literature: Poisson and logistic joinpoint models,
continuous joinpoints, covariates, jump and comparability ratio models
for coding changes, pairwise comparisons of trends, and clustering of
age groups.

Documentation, articles and the function reference are on the package
website: <https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/>.

![Six panels of age adjusted United States death rates from 1900 to
1998, one per cause of death, with fitted joinpoint models whose
segments are colored by trend direction and labeled with their annual
percent changes.](reference/figures/README-trend.png)

Six panels of age adjusted United States death rates from 1900 to 1998,
one per cause of death, with fitted joinpoint models whose segments are
colored by trend direction and labeled with their annual percent
changes.

## Installation

``` r

# Development version
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("skhademioore/joinpoint")
```

The grid search is compiled C++ (through Rcpp), so installing from
source needs a C++ toolchain:

- **macOS**: Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`)
- **Windows**: [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/)
- **Linux**: `g++` and `make` (usually present by default)

## Quick start

``` r

library(joinpoint)

fit <- joinpoint(us_mortality, x = year, y = rate, by = "cause", kmax = 3)
fit                      # joinpoints, APCs and AAPCs for each cause
apc(fit)                 # segment APCs with confidence intervals
aapc(fit)                # average annual percent changes
joinpoints(fit)          # joinpoint locations with confidence intervals
model_selection(fit)     # selection statistics for every model
jp_table(fit)            # formatted table for a manuscript

autoplot(fit, color_by = "trend", log_y = TRUE)
plot_apc(fit)
plot_aapc(fit)
```

## What is covered

| Method | Function or argument | Reference |
|----|----|----|
| Rates, age adjusted rates, proportions, percents, counts, other values | `joinpoint(type = )`, [`age_adjust()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/age_adjust.md) |  |
| Linear and log-linear models | `log =` | Kim et al. (2000) |
| Constant variance, standard errors, Poisson variance | `variance =` |  |
| First order autocorrelated errors (estimated or given), covariance matrix | `autocorrelation =`, `vcov =` |  |
| Exhaustive grid search with placement constraints and points between observations | `jp_control(min_obs_end, min_obs_between, n_grid)` | Lerman (1980) |
| Continuous joinpoints, exact least squares | `continuous = TRUE` | Hudson (1966) |
| Poisson and logistic joinpoint models, exact maximum likelihood, optional quasi-likelihood dispersion | `family =`, `overdispersion =` | Czajkowski et al. (2008) |
| Covariates such as seasonal terms | `covariates =` |  |
| BIC, BIC3, weighted BIC, data dependent selection | `method =` | Kim et al. (2023) |
| Modified BIC | `method = "mbic"` | Zhang and Siegmund (2007) |
| Sequential permutation test | `method = "permutation"` | Kim et al. (2000) |
| Sequential Monte Carlo likelihood ratio test | `method = "lrt"` | Czajkowski et al. (2008) |
| Early stopping of the Monte Carlo tests | `jp_control(n_exceed = )` | Besag and Clifford (1991) |
| Minimum APC difference worth detecting | `jp_control(madwd = )` |  |
| Parametric intervals: APC, AAPC, joinpoint location | `ci_method = "parametric"` | Clegg et al. (2009); Lerman (1980) |
| Empirical quantile intervals and p values | `ci_method = "empirical"` | Kim et al. (2017, 2022) |
| AAPC for the full range, last N observations and custom ranges | `jp_control(aapc_full, aapc_last, aapc_ranges)` | Clegg et al. (2009) |
| Exclusion of data points, shifted x values | `exclude =`, `shift =` |  |
| Jump model and comparability ratio model | `jump =`, `comparability_ratio =` | Chen et al. (2020) |
| Pairwise tests of parallelism and coincidence, AAPC comparison, multiplicity adjustment | [`jp_compare()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_compare.md) | Kim et al. (2004) |
| Multi-group clustering of age groups | [`jp_cluster()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_cluster.md) |  |
| Model estimates, covariance, goodness of fit (R squared, Durbin-Watson), data and export tables | [`model_estimates()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/model_estimates.md), [`vcov()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/vcov.html), [`model_selection()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/model_selection.md), [`as.data.frame()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/as.data.frame.html), [`jp_export()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_export.md) |  |

Not covered: Bayesian joinpoint models and joinpoint models for survival
or complex survey data.

The grid search is written in C++ and evaluates each candidate model
from cross products only, so permutation tests and empirical quantile
resampling over thousands of data sets run in seconds.

## Key functions

| Function | Purpose |
|----|----|
| [`joinpoint()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/joinpoint.md), [`jp_control()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_control.md) | Fit joinpoint models; search, selection and interval settings |
| [`apc()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/apc.md), [`aapc()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/apc.md), [`joinpoints()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/apc.md) | Segment APCs, AAPCs and joinpoint locations with confidence intervals |
| [`model_selection()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/model_selection.md), [`model_estimates()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/model_estimates.md), [`jump_estimates()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jump_estimates.md) | Selection statistics and tests, coefficients, jump and comparability ratio |
| [`jp_table()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_table.md) | Publication table of trends |
| [`coef()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html), [`vcov()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/vcov.html), [`fitted()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/fitted.values.html), [`residuals()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/residuals.html), [`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html), [`as.data.frame()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/as.data.frame.html) | Standard model methods |
| [`jp_compare()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_compare.md) | Pairwise tests of parallelism and coincidence, AAPC comparisons |
| [`jp_cluster()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_cluster.md), [`age_adjust()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/age_adjust.md) | Clustering of contiguous age groups; direct age adjustment |
| [`jp_export()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_export.md) | Every result table as delimited text |
| [`autoplot()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html), [`plot_apc()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/plot_apc.md), [`plot_aapc()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/plot_apc.md), [`plot_models()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/plot_models.md), [`plot_selection()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/plot_selection.md), [`plot_residuals()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/plot_residuals.md) | Figures |
| [`theme_joinpoint()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/theme_joinpoint.md), [`scale_color_joinpoint()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/theme_joinpoint.md), [`scale_fill_joinpoint()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/theme_joinpoint.md) | Theme and color scales of the figures |

## Validation

The test suite checks the package against published analyses and
independent computations:

- the 24 models of the joinpoint tutorial of van Doren (2024) on the US
  mortality data: every joinpoint location, and every published fitted
  value to its two decimals except eight transcription errors and eight
  cells inconsistent with their neighbors at the second decimal (each
  listed in the test); and the selections of its permutation test;
- the prepregnancy BMI analysis of Khademioore et al. (2026, Table 4):
  the BIC values, the joinpoint, the slopes, the segment p values and
  the slope change with its p value; the joinpoint interval is
  reproduced by the conservative variant of the parametric interval, and
  the slope intervals are not (they imply more degrees of freedom than
  the p values);
- brute force maximum likelihood for Poisson and binomial fits, fine
  grids for continuous joinpoints, and
  [`lm()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html) for covariate adjustment.

## Vignettes

Each vignette tells one analysis from question to figure. Read them on
the [package
website](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/articles/), or with
`vignette(package = "joinpoint")` after installation, in reading order:

*Getting started*

- [`vignette("joinpoint")`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/articles/joinpoint.html):
  a century of United States mortality, from a first fit to a manuscript
  table
- [`vignette("published-analysis")`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/articles/published-analysis.html):
  reproducing a published analysis of prepregnancy BMI in Ontario,
  quantity by quantity

*Methods*

- [`vignette("model-selection")`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/articles/model-selection.html):
  how many joinpoints? The selection rules, the permutation test, and
  joinpoints too small to matter
- [`vignette("uncertainty")`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/articles/uncertainty.html):
  how certain is a trend? Error models and parametric versus empirical
  quantile intervals
- [`vignette("comparing-groups")`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/articles/comparing-groups.html):
  did two trends move together? Tests of parallelism and coincidence
- [`vignette("coding-changes")`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/articles/coding-changes.html):
  breaks that are not trends, from outliers to coding changes
- [`vignette("clustering")`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/articles/clustering.html):
  which age groups share a trend? Age adjustment and clustering
- [`vignette("extensions")`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/articles/extensions.html):
  counts, seasons and joinpoints between observations

*Graphics*

- [Graphics
  gallery](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/articles/graphics-gallery.html)
  (website only): every figure the package draws, and how to adapt it
  for a paper, a slide or a report

## References

Besag J, Clifford P (1991). Sequential Monte Carlo p-values.
*Biometrika* 78:301-304.

Chen HS, Zeichner S, Anderson RN, Espey DK, Kim HJ, Feuer EJ (2020). The
joinpoint-jump and joinpoint-comparability ratio model for trend
analysis with applications to coding changes in health statistics.
*Journal of Official Statistics* 36:49-62.

Clegg LX, Hankey BF, Tiwari R, Feuer EJ, Edwards BK (2009). Estimating
average annual percent change in trend analysis. *Statistics in
Medicine* 28:3670-3682.

Czajkowski M, Gill R, Rempala G (2008). Model selection in logistic
joinpoint regression with applications to analyzing cohort mortality
patterns. *Statistics in Medicine* 27:1508-1526.

Hudson DJ (1966). Fitting segmented curves whose join points have to be
estimated. *Journal of the American Statistical Association*
61:1097-1129.

Khademioore S, Darling EK, D’Souza R, Muraca GM, Guo Y, Anderson LN
(2026). Prepregnancy body mass index in Ontario from 2012 to 2022: a
population-based descriptive study. *Canadian Journal of Public Health*.

Kim HJ, Fay MP, Feuer EJ, Midthune DN (2000). Permutation tests for
joinpoint regression with applications to cancer rates. *Statistics in
Medicine* 19:335-351.

Kim HJ, Fay MP, Yu B, Barrett MJ, Feuer EJ (2004). Comparability of
segmented line regression models. *Biometrics* 60:1005-1014.

Kim HJ, Luo J, Chen HS, et al. (2017). Improved confidence interval for
average annual percent change in trend analysis. *Statistics in
Medicine* 36:3059-3074.

Kim HJ, Chen HS, Byrne J, Wheeler B, Feuer EJ (2022). Twenty years since
Joinpoint 1.0: two major enhancements, their justification, and impact.
*Statistics in Medicine* 41:3102-3130.

Kim HJ, Chen HS, Midthune D, et al. (2023). Data-driven choice of a
model selection method in joinpoint regression. *Journal of Applied
Statistics* 50:1992-2013.

Lerman PM (1980). Fitting segmented regression models by grid search.
*Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C* 29:77-84.

van Doren T (2024). Estimating time points of significant change in
cause-specific mortality: joinpoint regression in R. *The Denominator*.
<doi:10.6069/JK1Y-7Z16>

Zhang NR, Siegmund DO (2007). A modified Bayes information criterion
with applications to the analysis of comparative genomic hybridization
data. *Biometrics* 63:22-32.

## Citing joinpoint

``` r

citation("joinpoint")
```

Releases will be archived on [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/) with a
citable DOI (the DOI badge appears after the first release). The
repository ships machine-readable citation and software metadata for
FAIR harvesters:

- [`CITATION.cff`](https://github.com/skhademioore/joinpoint/blob/main/CITATION.cff):
  Citation File Format (GitHub “Cite this repository”, Zenodo).
- [`codemeta.json`](https://github.com/skhademioore/joinpoint/blob/main/codemeta.json):
  CodeMeta 2.0 software metadata crosswalk.
- [`.zenodo.json`](https://github.com/skhademioore/joinpoint/blob/main/.zenodo.json):
  Zenodo deposit metadata (author, ORCID, license, related identifiers).
- [`ro-crate-metadata.json`](https://github.com/skhademioore/joinpoint/blob/main/ro-crate-metadata.json):
  RO-Crate 1.1 packaging and provenance.
- [`inst/CITATION`](https://github.com/skhademioore/joinpoint/blob/main/inst/CITATION):
  the R-level citation (`citation("joinpoint")`).

All carry the GPL-3.0-or-later SPDX identifier and the author’s ORCID.

# Package index

## Fit joinpoint models

Fit joinpoint models to one or more trend series, and control the grid
search, the model selection and the confidence intervals.

- [`joinpoint()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/joinpoint.md)
  : Fit joinpoint regression models
- [`jp_control()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_control.md)
  : Control settings for joinpoint fitting

## Trend estimates

Segment APCs, AAPCs and joinpoint locations with their confidence
intervals, model selection statistics, regression coefficients and a
table for a manuscript.

- [`apc()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/apc.md)
  [`aapc()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/apc.md)
  [`joinpoints()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/apc.md)
  : Trend estimates from a joinpoint fit
- [`jp_table()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_table.md)
  : Publication table of trends
- [`model_selection()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/model_selection.md)
  : Model selection results
- [`model_estimates()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/model_estimates.md)
  : Model estimates
- [`jump_estimates()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jump_estimates.md)
  : Jump and comparability ratio estimates

## Model methods

Standard methods for fitted joinpoint models.

- [`as.data.frame(`*`<joinpoint>`*`)`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/as.data.frame.joinpoint.md)
  : Observed and modeled values
- [`predict(`*`<joinpoint>`*`)`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/predict.joinpoint.md)
  : Predictions from a joinpoint fit
- [`vcov(`*`<joinpoint>`*`)`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/vcov.joinpoint.md)
  : Covariance of the segment parameters

## Comparing and clustering trends

Tests of parallelism and coincidence, direct age adjustment and
clustering of contiguous age groups.

- [`jp_compare()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_compare.md)
  : Pairwise comparison of joinpoint trends
- [`age_adjust()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/age_adjust.md)
  : Directly age adjusted rates
- [`jp_cluster()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_cluster.md)
  : Multi-group clustering of age specific trends

## Graphics

Publication quality figures built with ggplot2.

- [`autoplot(`*`<joinpoint>`*`)`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/autoplot.joinpoint.md)
  [`plot(`*`<joinpoint>`*`)`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/autoplot.joinpoint.md)
  : Plot a joinpoint fit
- [`plot_apc()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/plot_apc.md)
  [`plot_aapc()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/plot_apc.md)
  : Plot segment APCs and AAPCs
- [`plot_models()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/plot_models.md)
  : Plot all fitted models
- [`plot_selection()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/plot_selection.md)
  : Plot model selection
- [`plot_residuals()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/plot_residuals.md)
  : Residual diagnostics
- [`autoplot(`*`<jp_comparison>`*`)`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/autoplot.jp_comparison.md)
  : Plot a pairwise comparison
- [`theme_joinpoint()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/theme_joinpoint.md)
  [`scale_color_joinpoint()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/theme_joinpoint.md)
  [`scale_fill_joinpoint()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/theme_joinpoint.md)
  : Theme and color scales for joinpoint graphics

## Export

- [`jp_export()`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/jp_export.md)
  : Export joinpoint results

## Data sets

- [`us_mortality`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/us_mortality.md)
  : Age adjusted death rates for six causes, United States 1900 to 1998
- [`ontario_bmi`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/ontario_bmi.md)
  : Prepregnancy body mass index in Ontario, 2012 to 2021
- [`std_populations`](https://skhademioore.github.io/joinpoint/reference/std_populations.md)
  : Standard populations for age adjustment
